abstract: We introduce COMI-LINGUA, the largest manually annotated Hindi-English code-mixed dataset, comprising 125K+ high-quality instances across five core NLP tasks: Token-level Language Identification, Matrix Language Identification, Named Entity Recognition, Part-Of-Speech Tagging and Machine Translation. Each instance is annotated by three bilingual annotators, yielding over 376K expert annotations with strong inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss’ Kappa ≥\\geq 0.81). The rigorously preprocessed and filtered dataset covers both Devanagari and Roman scripts and spans diverse domains, ensuring real-world linguistic coverage. Evaluation reveals that closed-weight LLMs significantly outperform traditional tools and open-weight models in zero-shot settings. Notably, one-shot prompting consistently boosts performance across tasks, especially in structure-sensitive predictions like POS and NER. Fine-tuning open-weight LLMs on COMI-LINGUA demonstrates substantial improvements, achieving up to 95.25 F1 in NER, 98.77 F1 in MLI, and competitive MT performance, setting new benchmarks for Hinglish code-mixed text. COMI-LINGUA is publicly available at this URL11 1 [https://huggingface.co/datasets/LingoIITGN/COMI-LINGUA](https://huggingface.co/datasets/LingoIITGN/COMI-LINGUA "") Version 1.0, Updated till 15nd September 2025..

bibliographic.title: COMI-LINGUA: Expert Annotated Large-Scale Dataset for Multitask NLP in Hindi-English Code-Mixing
bibliographic.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025

content.problem: Existing Hindi-English (Hinglish) code-mixed resources are small, skewed toward the Roman script, narrow in task coverage, and often synthetically generated rather than human-annotated, leaving researchers without a large, high-quality benchmark for training and evaluating models on code-mixed NLP.
content.proposed_solution: The authors curate COMI-LINGUA, the largest expert-annotated Hinglish code-mixed dataset spanning five NLP tasks and both Devanagari and Roman scripts, and use it to benchmark traditional NLP tools and LLMs under zero-shot, one-shot, and fine-tuned settings.
content.algorithm_or_model: COMI-LINGUA dataset with LoRA fine-tuned open-weight LLMs (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, aya-expanse-8b, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct)
dataset_testbed: COMI-LINGUA (newly created expert-annotated Hinglish code-mixed dataset, 125,615 instances across five tasks)
raw text scraped from Indian news portals, X (Twitter), YouTube, and government archives, plus supplementary Hinglish samples from prior corpora (e.g., PHINC)
four NVIDIA Tesla V100 32 GB GPUs for fine-tuning and inference

content.claim: Fine-tuning open-weight LLMs on COMI-LINGUA brings substantial gains over prompting approaches and traditional tools, setting new benchmarks for Hinglish code-mixed NLP with up to 98.77 F1 on MLI and 95.25 F1 on NER.
author_stated_limitations: Findings from Hinglish code-mixed data may not generalize to other language pairs because of differences in syntax, sociolinguistic norms, and code-switching behavior.
The small, homogeneous annotator group may introduce demographic bias that limits the broader applicability and reliability of the annotations.
Scaling the work to other code-mixed language pairs is difficult due to the scarcity of high-quality annotated corpora and capable models.
The computational requirements and training-data needs of fine-tuning may limit accessibility for resource-constrained settings.

evidence.problem_quote: Despite growing interest, current Hinglish datasets have critical limitations: (1) a predominant focus on Roman script, ignoring natural script variation (Begum et al., 2016; Bali et al., 2014; Srivastava et al., 2020), (2) limited scale and coverage (Srivastava and Singh, 2021a; Kumar et al., 2018; Tiwari et al., 2024; Kartik et al., 2024), (3) insufficient task diversity (Aguilar et al., 2020; Khanujaa et al., 2020; Bohra et al., 2018; Khanuja et al., 2020), and (4) reliance on synthetic data generation and labeling rather than human annotation (Chatterjee et al., 2022; Srivastava and Singh, 2021c; Kartik et al., 2024; Sravani and Mamidi, 2023).
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: To address these limitations, we present a novel comprehensive dataset COMI-LINGUA (COde-MIxing and LINGuistic Insights on Natural Hinglish Usage and Annotation) that advances Hinglish code-mixing research.
evidence.claim_quote: Fine-tuning open-weight LLMs on COMI-LINGUA demonstrates substantial improvements, achieving up to 95.25 F1 in NER, 98.77 F1 in MLI, and competitive MT performance, setting new benchmarks for Hinglish code-mixed text.
author_stated_limitation_quotes: Language Pair Specificity: The findings derived from Hinglish code-mixed data may not generalize to other language pairs (e.g., Spanish-English), given differences in syntactic structure, sociolinguistic norms, and code-switching behavior.

Demographic Bias: The use of a relatively small and homogeneous group of annotators may introduce demographic bias, potentially limiting the broader applicability and reliability of the acceptability ratings.

Resource Constraints: Scaling this work to other code-mixed language pairs remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-quality annotated corpora and the limited availability of models capable of robustly handling diverse code-mixing phenomena.

Computational Accessibility: While fine-tuning shows substantial improvements, computational requirements and the need for substantial training data may limit accessibility for resource-constrained settings.
